newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Spain Uniban bank to approve Morocco merger.
newsitem.headline: Spain Uniban bank to approve Morocco merger.

text.p: Spanish Uniban bank will hold a meeting to approve its merger with Morocco's leading Wafabank, a bank spokesman said on Friday.
"Uniban will hold an ordinary general assembly on February 26, 1997 to examine and approve the convention of merger with Wafabank," the spokesman said.
Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Uniban or more than 2.46 million shares priced at about $28 million, a bourse official said.
A dispute between a minority group of shareholders over the shares parity and the management was behind a delay in the approval of the merger, a Casablanca-based broker said.
Wafabank is offering one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban while shareholders wanted one share against four, the broker added.
Uniban showed a 27.2 million dirhams ($2.9 million) loss in 1995 due mainly to provisions for non-performing debt, the bank said in a statement.
The bank in 1994 made losses of 44.01 million dirhams, it added but gave no updated figures for 1996.
The effective absorption of Uniban by Wafabank will take place by end March 1997, a bourse official said.
"The dissolution of Uniban and its delisting from the stock market after its merger with Wafabank will also be on the agenda of the bank's general assembly," the official said.

With a market capitalisation of more than 3.0 billion dirhams and one of the market's most liquid stocks, Wafabank made a net profit of 83 million dirhams in the first half of 1996 from 78.4 million dirhams in the same period in 1995.
Wafabank's turnover reached 801.5 million dirhams for the period of January-June 1996 from 711 million dirhams in the same period in 1995.
Wafabank and Uniban are among the 47 companies listed on the Casablanca bourse. Both banks were last traded at 630 dirhams and 129 dirham respectively
